speaker: Doctor
text: Hello there. Can you point to exactly where your leg hurts and tell me how long this has been bothering you?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old male. Mother has noticed a change in the child’s play patterns, specifically favoring his left leg while walking or running. The child complains of pain in his left knee, but denies any recent trauma or injury. He has no fever or other systemic symptoms. Nutrition and developmental milestones are appropriate for age.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does he have any pain in his left hip when you gently move his leg, and does the pain get worse at night?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain localized to the left knee. I also have Limping favoring left leg, No fever, No systemic symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Left Hip X-Ray
Does the pain in his knee radiate from his hip, and does he have limited internal rotation when you move his leg?

OBSERVATION_ATTACK.clean_observation: RESULTS: X-ray Left Hip Findings: Flattening and fragmentation of the left femoral head consistent with Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease. Musculoskeletal Examination: Tenderness on palpation of the left hip, not knee. Pain elicited with passive motion of the hip. Full range of motion in the knee. Negative for anterior drawer test and McMurray's.
